Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | First Invеstmеnt Updаtеs brоught tо уоu bу Іnception Media, LLC. South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.

# [Come on.](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=191586745&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTkxNTg2NzQ1LCJpYXQiOjE3NzQxMTE1OTAsImV4cCI6MTc3NjcwMzU5MCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.bOGeYkJ0vfYSxUSEvOrW0SNZFej2RPkQjyuqDjEDRFg)
### Utilities should not cash in while Michiganders get hit with bigger bills.
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| Mar 21
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9vcGVuLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9wdWIvaGFsZXlmb3JtaS9wL2NvbWUtb24_.yvXb9u3TNOesMgTc6NUsIge9cSScx_S47pLr_H_dujk?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/come-on?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

Hi friends,
Utility bills. We all have them. We all have to pay them. And we all keep an eye on them so we don't use too much.
That's why parents everywhere are still telling their kids to** "turn off the darn lights!"**__ when they leave a room.
But these essential utilities are driving a whole lot of Michiganders - including me - crazy.
Here's why: **Electricity bills keep going up, and too many working families are getting worse service in return.**
Let me repeat that: _Higher bills. Worse service._
I'm sorry, what the heck is happening? Because that's not right.
Here's the part that really drives me bananas: While hardworking folks are trying to keep up with their higher bills, corporate executives are getting richer off their backs.
That is totally unacceptable.
**That 's why I introduced new legislation to strip federal funding from investor-owned utilities that keep coming back for more rate hikes.**
Because let me just say the common-sense thing here: Executives should not get bigger checks while Michiganders get hit with bigger bills.
_**Come on.**_
There has to be some basic fairness in this equation.
If you are asking families to pay more again - _after they 've already been paying more_ - then maybe the people at the top shouldn't keep benefitting while everyone else gets squeezed.
Maybe federal dollars should not keep flowing with no strings attached.
**Maybe the government should actually look out for the people paying the bills, not the ones padding their own pockets.**
That's the part that really gets me. Too often in this country, the people doing the hardest work get the least help.
Working families are told to tighten their belts. Rural communities are told hospitals aren't feasible. Seniors are told skyrocketing medication prices are just a part of life.
But somehow, wealthy CEOs keep getting what they need.
Their executives get paid. Their investors get a higher return.
Meanwhile, regular people are left opening another utility bill and wondering what the heck they're supposed to cut back on this time.
Folks, that is not some abstract policy problem. **That is real life.**
That's groceries.
That's a doctor's visit.
That's a tank of gas.
That's why I'm fighting back.
Because government should not be in the business of making life easier for the wealthiest while making life harder for everyone else.
Government should work _for working_ people.
**I 'm running for Senate because I've seen what government can do when it's actually on the side of working people.**
I saw it when we helped save 200,000 Michigan jobs as Chief of Staff on President Obama's auto rescue in 2009. I see it when we invest in manufacturing and infrastructure today.
And I know it can be true here, too.
We can have a government that stands up to powerful companies and says: No, you do not get to keep raising costs on working families just to make your investors richer.
It's not revolutionary to say that Michigan families deserve affordable, reliable utilities.
They deserve fairness.
And they deserve leaders who are willing to say, plainly, when something is just not right.
**This is one of those times.**
With grit,
Haley
* * *

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?

I’m proud of my record: always standing up for working families and communities under attack. But many of my opponents can’t say the same.
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21486?t=1&akid=41016%2E3422442%2EJxKtOr)
Peter,
Who you are as a leader depends on the values you put first.
I’m proud of my record: always standing up for working families and communities under attack. But many of my opponents can’t say the same.
After Donald Trump unleashed federal agents on Los Angeles, my opponent **_Eric Swalwell voted to thank ICE._** And the billionaire in this race, Tom Steyer, **_made his billions partly by investing in the same private prisons that ICE is using right now to detain thousands of immigrants._**
**_I called to abolish ICE_** because I’ve always stood with immigrant communities.
And when it comes to protecting our environment from fossil fuel polluters, **I’m the only major candidate in this race who has never cashed a check or made a dollar from Big Oil.**
Meanwhile, Eric Swalwell just took the maximum contribution possible—nearly $40,000—from an oil company, **despite signing a public pledge to not take fossil fuel money.**
And Tom Steyer made some of his fortune by investing in Big Oil and other polluters.
Unlike my opponents, I don’t change my voice depending on how the political winds blow or sell out my values to the highest bidder, because what is right is right, _always_.
California’s next governor needs to be clear-eyed about protecting our state. That means standing up for our values no matter what. That’s exactly the type of governor I will be.

**Kathy Seiden Backs Letlow as Momentum Builds in Louisiana Senate Race**
_Latest endorsement underscores growing support for Trump-endorsed conservative Julia Letlow across the state._
**BATON ROUGE, LA** \- Congresswoman Julia Letlow, the Trump-endorsed candidate for U.S. Senate in Louisiana, announced she has received the endorsement of Kathy Seiden in her campaign for the United States Senate.
Seiden, a longtime conservative leader and advocate for Louisiana families, praised Rep. Letlow’s leadership, integrity, and record of delivering results for the state.
_“Julia Letlow is exactly the kind of leader Louisiana needs in the United States Senate,”_ **said Seiden.**_“She leads with conviction, faith, and a deep love for our state. Julia has proven she can bring people together, stand firm on conservative principles, and deliver meaningful results for our communities. I am proud to endorse her and look forward to helping her win this race.”_
Rep. Letlow thanked Seiden for her support and longstanding commitment to advancing conservative values across Louisiana.
_“I’m grateful for Kathy’s support and for the encouragement we’re continuing to see from across Louisiana,”_**said Rep. Letlow.** _“This campaign is about fighting for our state, protecting our values, and making sure Louisiana has strong, conservative leadership in Washington. I’m proud of the momentum we’re building and the people who are stepping up to be part of it.”_
Rep. Letlow currently represents Louisiana’s 5th Congressional District and serves on the House Appropriations Committee, where she has worked to secure key funding for infrastructure, disaster recovery, and economic development projects benefiting communities throughout Louisiana.
The Letlow campaign continues to gain support from leaders and grassroots conservatives statewide as the Senate race intensifies.
For more information, visit [JuliaLetlow.com](https://julialetlow.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=70758973fc60553eda6683b43&id=dcec4f6886&e=95355a072c).

| | | Mark Robert Gordon, a longtime voting and civil rights advocate, Democratic leader, and union activist, is running to flip Arizona’s 1st Congressional District.

[ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127794125/609225052/-195246293?refcode=20251227_em_fr_b1_MRG_eng&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTg4NTUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNTk1NjZkNjgtNDgyNS1mMTExLTlhNDgtMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=YoGF67clX5FoUSdJAC3hXLQhiILwCs8aKyAAK10Oo_8=)

Gordon grew up in north central Phoenix, the son of a disabled World War II veteran and a public school teacher. He attended Phoenix public schools and put himself through Princeton, Columbia Law and Harvard by working part-time jobs and earning scholarships.

For more than 30 years, Gordon has worked as a voting rights advocate and attorney, leading voter protection efforts nationwide and founding a voting rights organization dedicated to electing pro-democracy leaders. He has even taken that commitment abroad, delivering humanitarian aid to war-torn Ukraine on three missions.

A small business owner and proud union member for more than three decades, Gordon serves on the Democratic National Committee’s Small Business Council, where he advocates for policies that support workers and small businesses. He also serves on the Arizona AFL-CIO and Maricopa Area Labor Federation boards.

Gordon has been a Democrat his entire life and made it his mission to fight for everyday people, protect voting rights, and defend democracy at home and abroad.

Now, he’s running for Congress to finish that fight, for every Arizonan whose future is under attack by Donald Trump and David Schweikert.

body:
If James and I win, we can take back Texas this fall.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
On Friday in Fort Worth, I joined James Talarico and other Democratic leaders for an event focused on what Texans are demanding right now — **lower costs, strong public schools, reliable infrastructure, and leaders who show up and get the job done.**
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260321_1_event.3wXo_f&refcode=em20260321-790&amount=5&t=1&akid=790%2E299639%2EEXRcqE)
I left that event feeling energized, Peter: Texans are paying attention and showing they want leaders who will listen and deliver.

name: David Hogg
subject: “Which corporations are funding her campaign?”
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
This is proof that the work we’re doing really matters.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260321-1&t=1&akid=3273%2E587540%2ENiH2Jx)
Peter,
Back in 2024, Leaders We Deserve helped elect Texas State Senator Molly Cook by 62 votes. **That election was proof that the work we’re doing really matters.**
Recently in Houston, I ran into someone who reminded me how true that really is.
I’ve told this story before, but when I was out canvassing for Molly on Election Day in 2024, I knocked on the door of a 20-year-old named Kai who was completely skeptical. His first question: **“Which corporations are funding her campaign?”**
I was happy to tell him that the answer was _none of them,_ because _Leaders We Deserve only backs candidates who refuse contributions from corporate PACs._
When he learned that Molly was funded by grassroots supporters instead of corporations, his whole outlook changed. He went from suspicious to excited. He told me he had never voted in a primary before, but he decided to vote for Molly that day. I got his phone number for the campaign and texted him a few hours later to confirm he voted before the polls closed.
That night, when Molly won by only 62 votes, I remembered Kai and the other voters I’d met that day. Every single one of them made a difference in Molly’s win.
**Fast forward to a couple weeks ago in Houston:** After spending the day knocking doors for our candidate Christian Menefee ahead of his primary election, I joined Molly Cook for an event. During my speech, I told the story about meeting Kai back in 2024 while knocking doors for Molly’s primary race. **And I almost couldn’t believe it, but after my speech a young guy came over to me and I suddenly realized that Kai had been in the audience the whole time.**
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260321_1_kai.S8IS3C&refcode=em20260321-3273&amount=5&t=2&akid=3273%2E587540%2ENiH2Jx)
I was blown away, Peter. Seeing Kai that night meant he’d gone from a skeptical non-voter to someone who was at an off-year political event for his state senator.
He went from someone who had (rightfully) checked out of politics to someone who actually had a leader who spoke to him and gave him something to support.
If this doesn’t prove our whole theory, I don’t know what else does. Young people care deeply about our futures. But it’s hard for us to have faith in the same old failed leaders who have allowed the status quo to hold us back for literal decades.
We’re supporting bold young progressives who are inspiring young voters like Kai. That’s the movement we’re building with people like you who believe in this work.
**[If you’re with us, pitch in $5 or anything you can now to power our fight.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260321_1_kai.S8IS3C&refcode=em20260321-3273&amount=5&t=3&akid=3273%2E587540%2ENiH2Jx)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260321_1_kai.S8IS3C&amount=5&refcode=em20260321-3273&t=22&akid=3273%2E587540%2ENiH2Jx)**
Thank you for your support, Peter.
— David

| Peter, I released my annual financial disclosure form, and it only took me 5 minutes – because I don’t own any stocks.

And that’s exactly what Republicans love attacking me for: not being rich.

They can attack me all they want, but I have _no_ shame. Unlike them, I haven’t abused my office to get rich off stock trading.

When I ran for Congress, I drove for Uber and took on credit card debt just to get by. And after my swearing in, I got denied from apartments in D.C. because of my credit.

So it’s funny when I get called out for experiencing the struggles that working class Americans experience everyday – because shouldn’t we have more leaders who know what it’s like? I think if we did, Congress would work a lot better than it does now.

The first phase, targeting 800 megawatts and completion by early 2028, sits on former federal uranium land amid U.S. efforts to dominate AI infrastructure.

# Washington millionaire tax triggers huge marriage penalty
Washington state's **[new 9.9% income tax on earnings over $1 million,](https://substack.com/redirect/2069f825-9d7e-4aed-b1f6-3ad2d67b71bb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** passed by lawmakers and awaiting the governor's signature, applies a single threshold to households--creating the nation's largest marriage penalty, where dual earners face taxes that singles avoid. Critics warn it could drive wealth exodus from tech hubs.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2069f825-9d7e-4aed-b1f6-3ad2d67b71bb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Single Threshold Impact** : Unlike most states, the $1 million exemption doesn't double for married couples, hitting joint filers harder and sparking debate over fairness for dual-income professionals.
* **Potential Tax Bill Example** : A couple each earning $600,000 owes tax on $200,000 combined excess, while two singles at $1 million each pay nothing, highlighting the stark disparity.
* **Legislative Defense Offered** : Sen. Noel Frame justifies the structure for administrative simplicity, mirroring the state's capital gains tax approach despite criticism from tax experts.
* **Wealth Flight Concerns Rise** : Figures like Jeff Bezos and Howard Schultz already relocated citing taxes, with analysts predicting more high-earners may leave amid the new burden.

# Fraudster loses citizenship over $3.8M COVID Relief scam
A federal judge revoked the U.S. citizenship of Haitian-born Joff Stenn Wroy Philossaint **[after he orchestrated a $3.8 million COVID-19 relief fraud scheme in Florida,](https://substack.com/redirect/b6a2bc87-40ed-4f66-9f9d-9f15e9f35c00?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** lying during naturalization to conceal ongoing crimes between 2020 and 2021. He personally pocketed hundreds of thousands.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b6a2bc87-40ed-4f66-9f9d-9f15e9f35c00?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Fraud Scheme Execution** : Submitted dozens of false loan applications with fabricated revenue and payroll data, securing $3.8 million total and receiving about $549,000 personally.
* **Naturalization Deception Revealed** : Denied crimes or false statements in a 2020 sworn interview, yet obtained citizenship in 2021 while fraud continued undetected initially.
* **Legal Revocation Basis** : Court ruled he procured citizenship illegally through false pretenses, allowing revocation even without prior conviction for the fraud.
* **Consequences Imposed** : Faces serious prison time for the scheme, with citizenship stripped per federal prosecutors in Southern District of Florida.

I voted NO on all of these bills , which would make it harder for students to access scholarships and financial aid, insert federal politics into local classroom decisions, and make it tougher for workers like school staff and bus drivers to enforce their rights. As an educator, I know what actually helps kids learn: stable classrooms, mental health supports, special-education services, and fully funded Title I resources. That is what I am working to defend in Congress. I have seen firsthand how a quality education can lift people out of a poverty cycle and put them on a pathway to success. I will not stand by and allow Congress to leave our students behind. name: Jon Ossoff
subject: Broken promises
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY SCHIFF FOR SENATE
body:
| [](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/6034?t=3&akid=9658%2E5257348%2EB2QMan) See, I get why some folks voted for Trump. He promised to attack a broken system. And it’s a ripe target. Even before Trump came on the scene, America had one of the most corrupt political systems in the Western world. It’s been running on corporate money, secret money, billionaire money. And it’s worse than ever now. _Citizens United_ was the worst court decision in modern American history. When Members of Congress aren’t begging for money from Washington lobbyists, they’re trying to dodge getting carpet-bombed by super PACs. Senators get threatened with millions of dollars of attack ads over the votes they take. And see, that is why things don’t work for ordinary people. It’s because the people’s elected representatives don’t represent the people. They represent the big donors! That corruption is why they defunded nursing homes to cut taxes for the rich. Corruption is why you pay a fortune for prescriptions. Corruption is why your insurance claim keeps getting denied. Corruption is why hedge funds get to buy up all the houses in your neighborhood, and then your corporate landlord ignores your calls during a gas leak. Corruption is why that ambulance costs $3,000 after you just had to get your choking toddler to the hospital. Yes, the system really is rigged. But Trump’s not unrigging it. He’s re-rigging it for himself! He’s a crook and a con man, and he wants to be a king. You can’t claim to be for ordinary men and women when you defund their hospitals and nursing homes. You can’t claim to be for ordinary men and women when you defund school lunch programs to help feed little boys and little girls whose hard-working parents are struggling to fill the fridge. You can’t claim to be for ordinary men and women when you do these things so you can cut taxes for the richest people in the country while you and your family business rake in massive sums from around the world. Donald Trump’s second term has already done unfathomable damage to our country and the lives of millions of people. And the people are beginning to see it. But only by regaining Congressional power can we stop him. Really. The upcoming 2026 midterms are our last chance to restore checks and balances. And my Senate race in Georgia is the single most critical contest: I’m the only Democratic Senator up for reelection in 2026 in a state Trump carried in 2024. So if you’re outraged by what’s happening to our country — and you’re ready to fight for the future of this Republic –– please don’t wait until 2028: Split a donation of $10 between Adam Schiff and my reelection campaign in Georgia right now. Here’s the link to donate: [**secure.actblue.com/donate/abs-em-ossoff**](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/6034?t=4&akid=9658%2E5257348%2EB2QMan) The average online donation to our campaign is around $30. Please give what you can. All that matters is that lots and lots of people are contributing what they can to power our grassroots campaign before the end of the year. [**Please, contribute today.**](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/6034?t=5&akid=9658%2E5257348%2EB2QMan) Jon Ossoff | [DONATE](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/6034?t=6&akid=9658%2E5257348%2EB2QMan)

From rising costs at home to instability abroad, too many families are feeling the squeeze, while corporate CEOs and Wall Street bigwigs are more comfortable than ever. I wish I could promise that things will turn around overnight. But I won’t pretend that’s the case. **Friend,**
Derek Tran stood in Buena Park last week and said that **"unnecessary wars"** are why your groceries cost too much.
I have to be honest with you. That word stopped me cold.
_Unnecessary._
I was five years old when my father woke us up in the middle of the night. No explanation. Just — move. He had found a fishing boat. He had heard there was a way out of Vietnam, and he had decided that whatever it cost, it was worth it. He hid our family on that boat. We floated in the South China Sea for three days. No food. No promise anyone was coming. Just the dark water and my father's hands and the hope that somewhere out there, someone still believed freedom was worth fighting for.
A German tanker finally found us. We survived.
Was that war unnecessary? Were the boat people unnecessary? Were the 800,000 Vietnamese refugees who risked everything just to breathe free air — were they an overreaction?
I have lived the answer to that question. I carry it in my bones.
Derek Tran wants to represent a district where tens of thousands of families have a story just like mine. He wants the votes of people who know — _really know_ — what it means when the world decides a conflict isn't worth having. And he's standing there telling them it's all just noise. It's all just politics. It's all just "unnecessary."
I cannot let that go unanswered.
I am running for Congress because I believe America's strength is not something to be ashamed of. Because I have seen what happens to people — to families, to children — when that strength retreats. Because the Vietnamese-American community in Little Saigon deserves a representative who doesn't just understand their history politically — but **personally**.
I am that person. I have always been that person.
But I need your help to win.

When my family arrived in Huntington Beach in 1987, my dad had $20 in his pocket. That was everything. He stretched it into a life — a business, a family, a future. He taught me that $20, in the right hands, goes a long way.

Peter,

From the greatness of Mount Rainier to the North Cascades to Lake Chelan, Washington's Eighth District holds some of the most beautiful scenery in the country. Each one of these natural landscapes is what makes our home so special. They are places we love to take our children, where we can get outdoors and connect with nature.

Today, on International Day of Forests, we want to show you just how much Kim is fighting for our district and our environment. Just this month, Kim introduced a bipartisan bill aimed at protecting our forests and doing preventative work to ensure we stay out of harm's way from wildfires and other national disasters.

The Reforestation, Nurseries, and Genetic Resources (RNGR) Support Act of 2026 would codify the existing United States Forest Service’s RNGR program to ensure long-term support for our forests. It would help mitigate damage from pests, disease, and climate change. And it would help local nurseries increase their capacity so they can contribute more toward a healthy ecosystem of our forest lands.

This isn't the first time Kim has sought to protect our forests, and it won't be the last. She has worked tirelessly to expand protective measures, such as prescribed fires, to decrease the damage during tough fire seasons. She has sought funding for more training and research into how to best serve our communities. **And the majority of her efforts have been met with bipartisan support.**

But we're facing an administration that would rather denounce climate change and endanger our ecosystems than work to protect the beauty of WA-08 and the Americans whose job it is to protect our lands. Immediately after taking office, over 3,000 employees of the Forest Service were laid off at Trump's direction. And current budget proposals include cuts of up to $4 billion to federal land management agencies.

Protecting our forests isn't just about enhancing the beauty of our district. Every fire we contain saves a family's home. Every chance we get to stop smoke and debris from entering our air helps children with asthma breathe easier. And every researcher or biologist whose job we save ensures our forests can thrive.

body:
Thirteen years ago today, Colorado's Civil Union Act became law.

[ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127797321/609234392/-1473932214?refcode=logo&amount=10&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmMzlmYjVjZS00ZjI1LWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=7GnkRC5NA9WC76CYCJov6pIxXzFCyeMcU_fSg3y2mAk=) Folks, Thirteen years ago today, we signed Colorado's Civil Union Act into law, legislation that allowed same-sex couples to enter into civil unions. We even called lawmakers back for a special legislative session — and signing it was one of my proudest moments as Governor. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127797322/609234393/1664162816?amounts=5,15,25,50,100,250&refcode=email_032126_civilunion&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmMzlmYjVjZS00ZjI1LWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=7GnkRC5NA9WC76CYCJov6pIxXzFCyeMcU_fSg3y2mAk=)
_Here we are at the signing of Colorado’s Civil Union Act on March 21, 2013!_ **As Mayor of Denver, Governor of Colorado, and now as our U.S. Senator, we’ve always stood with the LGBTQ+ community.** In the Senate, we protected marriage equality nationwide through our _Respect for Marriage Act._ We guaranteed that same-sex and interracial couples have the same rights afforded to all other marriages. Last year, we reintroduced the _Equality Act,_ which bans discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity in housing, education, employment, public accommodations, federal funding, and more. And we’ve reintroduced the bipartisan _Refund Equality Act_ to make sure that married same-sex couples can amend their tax returns back to the date of their marriage. Who you love shouldn’t determine how you’re taxed. But while we’re fighting for equality for all, our MAGA opponent Mark Baisley is not. Baisley has made heartless comments about his LGBTQ+ colleagues in the state legislature, describing them as having “a brokenness in their minds” and claiming that they are “in rebellion against nature.” He’s introduced legislation to roll back our progress and ban gay marriage in Colorado. That’s not what we stand for here in Colorado. We can’t let someone like this ever represent our state in the U.S. Senate. **Love is love is love. Colorado will always fight for everyone to be free to love who they love and be who they are. We will never stop fighting for a more equal world for our LGBTQ community._[If you’re with us, please chip in now to help keep Colorado blue and stand up to the far-right extremists looking to roll back the progress we’ve fought so hard for.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127797323/609234394/1664162816?amounts=5,15,25,50,100,250&refcode=email_032126_civilunion&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmMzlmYjVjZS00ZjI1LWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=7GnkRC5NA9WC76CYCJov6pIxXzFCyeMcU_fSg3y2mAk=)_** _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | | | [Donate $5 →](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127797324/609234395/1664162816?express_lane=true&amounts=5,15,25,50,100&amount=5&refcode=email_032126_civilunion&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmMzlmYjVjZS00ZjI1LWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=7GnkRC5NA9WC76CYCJov6pIxXzFCyeMcU_fSg3y2mAk=)

clean_body: Thirteen years ago today, Colorado's Civil Union Act became law. = Folks, Thirteen years ago today, we signed Colorado's Civil Union Act into law, legislation that allowed same-sex couples to enter into civil unions. We even called lawmakers back for a special legislative session — and signing it was one of my proudest moments as Governor. = Here we are at the signing of Colorado’s Civil Union Act on March 21, 2013! As Mayor of Denver, Governor of Colorado, and now as our U.S. Senator, we’ve always stood with the LGBTQ+ community. In the Senate, we protected marriage equality nationwide through our Respect for Marriage Act. We guaranteed that same-sex and interracial couples have the same rights afforded to all other marriages. Last year, we reintroduced the Equality Act, which bans discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity in housing, education, employment, public accommodations, federal funding, and more. And we’ve reintroduced the bipartisan Refund Equality Act to make sure that married same-sex couples can amend their tax returns back to the date of their marriage. Who you love shouldn’t determine how you’re taxed. But while we’re fighting for equality for all, our MAGA opponent Mark Baisley is not. Baisley has made heartless comments about his LGBTQ+ colleagues in the state legislature, describing them as having “a brokenness in their minds” and claiming that they are “in rebellion against nature.” He’s introduced legislation to roll back our progress and ban gay marriage in Colorado. That’s not what we stand for here in Colorado. We can’t let someone like this ever represent our state in the U.S. Senate. Love is love is love. Colorado will always fight for everyone to be free to love who they love and be who they are. That’s why my team in Georgia is getting ready to engage millions of voters about what’s at stake in this election and what it will take to keep this Senate seat out of Trump’s and MAGA’s grubby hands.

And it’s why I’m asking for your help to make sure my team has the resources to do that work.

| | | | High school dropout. Waffle House waitress. First woman to graduate from The Citadel. Single mom. Fighter.

Nancy Mace wasn’t born into power. She worked for every inch of ground she’s gained.

At 17, she dropped out of high school and took a job slinging hash browns at Waffle House to survive. No silver spoon. No Ivy League connections. Just grit, grace, and a whole lot of graveyard shifts.

By the grace of God, she turned that struggle into a story no politician can touch. She made history as the first woman to graduate from The Citadel, South Carolina’s legendary military college. She built her own business. She raised two kids on her own. And when the Left came for everything she believed in, she stood her ground. Now, she’s running for Governor of South Carolina.

Nancy Mace is a battle-tested conservative who’s walked through fire and come out swinging. In Congress, she’s been one of President Trump’s fiercest allies, fighting to secure our border, protect our daughters, and stop the Left’s sick agenda dead in its tracks.

She’s not here to make friends. She’s here to make history.

Nancy is fighting to:

* Eliminate South Carolina’s Income Tax—the highest in the Southeast

* Prosecute violent criminals and pedophiles with zero leniency

* Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free

* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate

* Reform education so students learn how to think—not what to think

* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Through every hardship, Nancy never gave up. And now she’s ready to do what she’s always done: roll up her sleeves, take the heat, and lead from the front.

South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.

Team,
I’m relaunching my Substack.
This will be a space for policy deep dives, behind-the-scenes updates from the campaign trail, and real conversations about what Michiganders need in their next Senator.
**[If you want to help shape our priorities and hear the thinking behind our plans, sign up to join our Substack:](https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/signup/MAM-2026-Substack-Signup1?refcode=AU_MAM_EG_GEN_GEN_AC_20260321_PM1_V1_S1&t=2&akid=4269%2E898137%2Eyk4FSw)**

---
I’m running for the U.S. Senate because I believe Washington needs a little more Michigan fight. Most of us have done everything right and still can’t get ahead. The status quo doesn’t work...and it hasn’t for a long time. But while Donald Trump wants to burn it all to the ground, it’s on us to build something new, something that actually works for all of us.
**This Substack is my way of keeping the door open.** I want to use this platform to move past the jargon to talk about what it actually looks like to run a statewide campaign in one of the most-watched US Senate races in the country and to build a New American Dream.
I’ll be sharing:

* Behind-the-scenes updates from the campaign trail
* Stories from the road — from our brewery tours, volunteers, and the parents I meet at the park
* My personal reflections and reasoning behind the decisions I make on this campaign

We are not powerless. We can fight, we can win, and we can build something better — as long as we do it together.
**[Join us on Substack here.](https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/signup/MAM-2026-Substack-Signup1?refcode=AU_MAM_EG_GEN_GEN_AC_20260321_PM1_V1_S1&t=4&akid=4269%2E898137%2Eyk4FSw)**

I’m excited to write more, hear from you, and build a conversation that actually helps us win for Michigan.
Thanks,
Mallory

body:
| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127797956/609236267/734816049?&refcode=E28868-20260320-MaryPeltola-Image-Surrogate&amount=5&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS8xMDMxMTgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYmQ2NWRiMGQtNTMyNS1mMTExLTlhNDgtMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=4tccqaqvwixnYDhFYfOuEa2nXkz1_I_n2d08sfC2FGI=) In a moment, I’m going to ask you to [_**split a donation between Josh Harder and my campaign for U.S. Senate to help us win this fight for our future.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127797957/609236268/734816049?&refcode=E28868-20260320-MaryPeltola-SL-Surrogate&amount=5&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS8xMDMxMTgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYmQ2NWRiMGQtNTMyNS1mMTExLTlhNDgtMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=4tccqaqvwixnYDhFYfOuEa2nXkz1_I_n2d08sfC2FGI=) But first, let me explain why your support is so important using one of my favorite Alaska winter activities _– and our official state sport!_ When I was growing up, salmon fishing in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance. I still love to be outside. It reminds me of being a kid. But the abundance I remember doesn’t exist anymore. Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity. Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find. So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families. I’m tired of politicians in DC doing nothing to stop it. All while they profit off that very same system. That’s why I’m running to fight for Alaska’s future. Systemic change is the only way to fill our homes with abundance again. But it won’t be a smooth course to the finish line. We’re racing against corporate donors and dark money groups who are going to spend big because they don’t want the rigged system to change. They’re the only ones this broken system is working for! _So here’s where the lessons I learned from dog mushing come in:_**As long as we’re all pulling in the same direction, we can win this.** It’s all about the team, and I know we have an amazing grassroots movement that can take this on. Thousands of people have already pitched in to help us win this seat because they want to unrig the system in DC. clean_body: | | = In a moment, I’m going to ask you to = But first, let me explain why your support is so important using one of my favorite Alaska winter activities – and our official state sport! When I was growing up, salmon fishing in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance. I still love to be outside. It reminds me of being a kid. But the abundance I remember doesn’t exist anymore. Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity. Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find. So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families. I’m tired of politicians in DC doing nothing to stop it. All while they profit off that very same system. That’s why I’m running to fight for Alaska’s future. Systemic change is the only way to fill our homes with abundance again. But it won’t be a smooth course to the finish line. We’re racing against corporate donors and dark money groups who are going to spend big because they don’t want the rigged system to change. They’re the only ones this broken system is working for! So here’s where the lessons I learned from dog mushing come in:As long as we’re all pulling in the same direction, we can win this. It’s all about the team, and I know we have an amazing grassroots movement that can take this on. subject: What we’re not supposed to be talking about
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
Trump’s illegal war is an attempt to distract us, while life for working people keeps getting harder and harder.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260321-6033-footer&t=1&akid=6033%2E420207%2ERTHC9s)
Peter,
22 days into a war that no one asked for, and I needed to get this off my chest:
[](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260321.Pi_ZD7&refcode=em20260321-6033&t=2&akid=6033%2E420207%2ERTHC9s)
**Trump is counting on us to be distracted. To be so caught up by the chaos of this illegal war that we stop demanding answers from this administration and forget what we were already fighting for.**
Because the reality is: Prices are still crushing working families, the Epstein files are still being buried, and the corruption rampant in this administration didn’t disappear the moment Trump forced this country into a reckless, unconstitutional war.
And while all that is happening at home, 13 American servicemembers have already lost their lives, and hundreds more have been injured. Trump chose this path.
I got into this fight because I believe working people deserve better. Better than coverups, better than distractions, better than a president who campaigned on ending forever wars going back on his word a year later. That hasn’t changed. And neither has my commitment to calling it out, every single day, for as long as it takes.
[**If you’re able, will you pitch in $3 to help keep me in this fight — against an unconstitutional war that has already cost servicemembers their lives, and a president using war to escape accountability for the challenges working people are facing right here at home?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260321.Pi_ZD7&refcode=em20260321-6033&amount=3&t=3&akid=6033%2E420207%2ERTHC9s)

In solidarity,

name: Chip Roy
subject: They tried to buy this race
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY TEXANS FOR CHIP ROY
body:
A self-funder spent millions trying to buy this race. Texans said not so fast. |
_**Are you still with me, Fellow Patriot?**_

Nearly two million Texans cast a ballot in the Republican Primary for Attorney General - and thanks to the grassroots, we're headed to a runoff.

_But let's be honest about what happened in the first round._

My opponent tried to buy this race outright.

He poured more than $16 million of his own money into the campaign and outspent us **_3 to 1_** just to reach **_39%_** of the vote.

On top of that, a left-wing California PAC spent millions attacking me because they're furious about my work with President Trump to rip hundreds of billions of dollars in Green New Scam subsidies out of the so-called "Big Beautiful Bill."

They thought enough money could drown out the truth.

_They were wrong._

Because Texans know something that the political class and out-of-state donors don't:

[](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=61046504774144ecb9357511a0190ed1&_e=hzvopLkqQVeRo9swNGjPMcTT9IYdQuTU4DtAw0L8412cQcYWG2PvH4v7hSLfpSpfWStUom2hgZ6V8x5-C_jtnneUaW0Rx9TT1mHzFMXbC7Z_2OwFqlqg7K_sO1KkMzvMlwP6OTjyJ2QC4SPYaIcaJ1PQEqDFnvU-AmHdHbqKkr2nbVURvws-OAloYSkNeWb_PwEds2u9vJhgfWHe74MienuaZmUJe_P9Fff1qdBR0rRgH_vvxgiNGjOPUYsVrfPPXpKbcxoJHooLSc6xKIKiX0JOOAVwO7nFFiOTyQzJsb4paP-FXnQelZzmuqr6yfsIj5kQJJhKw1jWO85T3Vw1KIUX8w530eSMBxYTCHLL6gPZTCYepAXRew0Hm5Tun8IHq9MBXKncDdo0iU5HN34hA8ymHQvkY2aSl_iyD1jJPwn6eVcx1YPEed6LNMVsGj4X_aaF2jocK4U3SNZSyB4A_ThVwJUHchgWIG3shF5kXj7ch9H70WD9IvVJ_-NQzKT99VWJ34Je1o02cPbmpnuQJVZCcE91RM9Z65NPq_QmAShs002f9NCBVPSj8X9ScZ9nybA90tzgR9S0mc5oQ17771wd77_h7Wzh_q9Q632ZK3NIr0SC-3oX6vhO70xd6w51SeimqbrZ-WGfgDCQEehzSIlmAkuA37Ikuv30SlpA7rY%3D)
Now the runoff begins - and the stakes couldn't be higher.

The Attorney General of Texas must be ready on **DAY ONE** to defend our state against:
* A broken immigration system and open-border policies
* Hostile foreign nations buying Texas land
* The growing threat of radical Islam
* A future Democratic administration trying to reopen the floodgates of illegal immigration

This job isn't a stepping stone. It's the Chief Legal Officer for the largest conservative state in America.

# Real quick
### RE... Rep. Steve Tanner (Nampa, ID)
| | | [Brian Lenney](https://substack.com/@brianlenney)
---

They didn't learn...
After getting their asses _absolutely handed to them_ in both the 2022 and 2024 Idaho Republican primaries, the establishment hacks apparently decided the problem was they just hadn't tried enough dumb mailers.
Because that's what they did. Flooded the zone with them. Mailer after mailer after mailer, and voters still beat them like a rented mule, twice in a row.
So what's the move now? Another mailer against Rep. Steve Tanner, Nampa, District 13.
And it's stupid on multiple levels:

I’m Dr. Annie Andrews, a pediatrician, a mom of three, and the Democrat running for U.S. Senate to defeat Republican Lindsey Graham in South Carolina.
If we flip this seat, we can end Lindsey Graham’s career and help Democrats retake the Senate, and expand the map for Democrats in future elections.
I know this won’t be easy. But I’ve treated kids who were shot, hospitalized, and failed by broken systems. Nothing about this moment feels optional.
We need an overwhelming surge of grassroots support to prove that we can finally defeat Lindsey Graham. So I’m humbly asking: Will you chip in a split donation of $50, $30, or even $15 between Resist Reclaim Rebuild and my campaign right now so we can hit our end of quarter goals? >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-annieandrews] [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-annieandrews]
HELP ME DEFEAT LINDSEY GRAHAM! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-annieandrews]
Let me introduce myself.
I’ve spent nearly 20 years serving my community as a pediatrician, treating everything from asthma and violent trauma to the emotional toll of growing up in poverty.
I’ve seen what bad policy does to good families — and I’ve seen kids suffer because people like Lindsey Graham would rather protect their own power than protect children.
In 2022, after 15 years of working in hospitals, I ran for Congress because I knew our kids needed a voice in Washington. I lost — and I told my oldest daughter I wouldn’t run again.
But then Trump’s chaos came back.
And Lindsey Graham? He cheered.
The truth is, I’m scared. And I’m angry. And I’m done waiting.
So I’m stepping up — because our kids, and this country can’t afford another six years of Lindsey Graham.
I’m building a people-powered campaign to flip South Carolina and give kids the voice they deserve. And I need your help. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-annieandrews]
CHIP IN TO STOP MAGA EXTREMISM!>> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-annieandrews]

The Left thinks they OWN your kids...
Check out this small clip from a hearing on Friday about Idaho schools secretly transing your kids. We passed a bill to say they can't. Some leftists showed up in droves to oppose it:
[](https://substack.com/redirect/3c2c85c8-0618-4d5f-bad1-3ba6e0b78277?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This should not surprise anyone...
And it's part of a several-decade-long trend to take away parenting from parents and outsource it to the schools, the state, even social media. Or how about a combo of all three?
Because yesterday, the House and Senate passed a bill to make billion-dollar social media companies AND the state of Idaho the new Mommy and Daddy.
[H0542. The "Stop Harms from Addictive Social Media Act."](https://substack.com/redirect/72f45ff6-c4b3-4bec-8ab4-4120fc95dc6e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Sounded great, right? Protect kids from Instagram and TikTok?!
Except I voted no, and here's why (full debate, my part starts at 13 minutes):
[](https://substack.com/redirect/a194901f-b545-4251-8a09-0460afe5744f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
We all want to protect kids...
I think to some extent, every single person in that chamber does (although, obviously we all define it differently and have different goalposts).
This bill (H542), to its credit, was aimed in the right direction. Because it didn't go after app stores or device manufacturers._It targeted the platforms themselves._ That was the right call. And Meta came out against it (they had five lobbyists running around the building trying to kill it, from what I heard).
So let's look at who was lobbying against this bill:
1. The Washington Post reported in August 2025 that [Instagram's chatbot helped teen accounts plan suicide (and parents can't disable it)](https://substack.com/redirect/08c88e59-454b-4a7f-8bf0-63e2d478e17e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
2. Court documents from last month showed an [internal Meta researcher warned of 500,000 child sexual exploitation cases per day](https://substack.com/redirect/b179ad21-52f6-44c2-95ef-5ca574402407?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), English-speaking markets only, and their own employee wrote "we expect the true situation is worse."
3. TIME Magazine reported that [Meta had a 17-strike policy for sex trafficking](https://substack.com/redirect/bd2315cb-6dc7-46b9-bacc-843a497111ae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Sixteen violations before your account got suspended. Their former head of safety testified to this under oath.

That's who was fighting this bill.
But here was my problem...
_**I 'm also old enough to remember when conservatives said "we don't co-parent with the government."**_
And although I really wanted this to work, I couldn't vote for it. Because it was presented as a bill that _ "put parents in the driver's seat" _and _" protected kids"_ but the kids who needed this most got nothing!
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4668870e-9360-42b0-bd8c-531292725ea5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Section 48-2103(2) says these platforms have no obligation to verify age on accounts that existed continuously for seven years.
Say your daughter lied about her age at ten and has been on Instagram ever since. The algorithm shaped her entire adolescence. Eating disorder content at midnight, comparison culture wrecking her self-image, all of it.
By seventeen this bill owes her nothing! The Left thinks they OWN your kids...

Parents don't need a bill to put them in the driver's seat.
They're already there.
**Because your thirteen-year-old doesn 't have a phone unless you bought it. Instagram? You allowed that. You can take it away tonight if you want. No bill required.**
But Section 48-2103 requires platforms to track cumulative usage. Twenty-five hours, fifty hours, every hundred hours after that. Detailed usage histories tied to identifiable users. That's a surveillance apparatus for your kid. Run by the same companies that connected groomers to two million minors. And now we're trusting them to protect your daughter?!
And this is where it got insulting to me...
Section 48-2106(3) says parents can't waive the requirements. You understand the risks, you make an informed choice about your own child, and the state says nope. Your judgment doesn't count.
So we mandated that billion-dollar social media companies monitor your children for you. While overriding your authority to make decisions about your own family.
Because apparently parenting is too hard and the government knows better.
**That 's not conservative. **
**I don 't know what it is but it's not that.**

---|---|---
And then there's the compliance theater aspect of all this..
Section 48-2105(2)(d) says platforms aren't liable if they used "reasonable means" to comply.
Meta's lawyers are going to camp out in those two words. So will TikTok's. So will every platform with a legal team. Every violation will turn into a multiyear court fight about what "reasonable" means.
Meanwhile your kid keeps scrolling. Not protected.
They already know who these kids are. They target ads to thirteen-year-old girls interested in fitness with surgical precision. But now they have a legal excuse to play dumb.
The thirty-day loophole is almost "funny" too...
Section 48-2104(7)(b) says when a platform flags a child's account, the kid gets thirty days to dispute. Infinite scroll stays on during that window. Autoplay too. The exact features we're supposedly banning keep running while compliance happens on paper.
**Imagine you find out a kid is being abused in a group home. You don 't remove them for thirty days because the home needs time to "dispute the findings." That kid stays in the same environment, same exposure, same harm, while paperwork gets shuffled around.**
That's what this bill does. We identified the harm. We just gave it a month to keep happening.
And the billion-dollar threshold? Discord walks. Tumblr walks. Roblox probably walks too (they make their money from Robux, not ads, and this bill only covers advertising revenue). The next TikTok walks. Any platform under a billion in ad revenue operates freely while Meta and Snapchat build compliance systems their competitors can't afford.
So really, we just protected their market position and called it regulation.
All these billion-dollar corporations have to do is hire some compliance officers, build a dashboard, let the lawyers handle the edge cases. The ones who can't afford it? Free pass.
_**Kids on Discord? Unprotected.**_
_**Kids on Roblox? Unprotected.**_
But Meta, TikTok, and Snapchat get a compliance shield and calls it a win.

Derek, it’s official!

Last night, I won the Democratic nomination for North Carolina’s U.S. Senate seat. I’ll be running against Republican Michael Whatley, a far-right Big Oil lobbyist and President Trump’s handpicked candidate.

As I start my general election campaign, I’m thinking about how grateful I am for the support of folks like you that got me here. This is the time to stand up and fight for our future – and I am ready. But I need you with me.

My team and I have set a goal to raise $1 million before Thursday at midnight to kick off the general election campaign. Will you split a gift between our campaign and John Fetterman of $5 today to help us win the biggest Senate race in the country, break the GOP’s hold on Washington and return power to the people?

https://act.johnfetterman.com/go/52963?t=1001&akid=10653%2E434096%2EsRnkr_

I didn’t plan to run for federal office. I wanted to serve North Carolina from right here at home. But when I look at what’s happening across the country, I know I can’t leave things as they are for my daughters or for yours.

So long as Trump’s extreme allies are in power, there is no path to accountability or restraint. Just more chaos, division and attacks on our fundamental freedoms.

To set our nation back on course, we must regain Senate control – and that starts by winning in North Carolina. We can flip this seat from red to blue for the first time since 2008, but far-right Republican PACs and megadonors will spend hundreds of millions to stop us.

Whether they succeed depends on people like you, Derek, stepping up to help us hit our goal before Thursday night. Will you split a gift between our campaign and John Fetterman of $5 or whatever you can today to help us reach our general election fundraising goal and build the momentum we need to win?

https://act.johnfetterman.com/go/52963?t=1002&akid=10653%2E434096%2EsRnkr_

Thank you for everything.

Roy

This weekend, the U.S. Senate is in session debating the SAVE Act--legislation that would require proof of citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.
While that debate unfolds in Washington, here in Connecticut, our priorities tell a very different story.
Connecticut's five Democrat Congressmen and two Democrat Senators--are fighting against the SAVE Act in Washington D.C., calling voter verification "Jim Crow 2.0."
That is despite about overwhelming support even demonstrated on a CNN poll showing all "major" demographics:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/cac00b29-6c2d-46f6-985f-45909665e36a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[Source](https://substack.com/redirect/db020f81-900f-4689-a748-5ea1a8e47478?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
At the very same time, CT leaders in Hartford rushed through an emergency Senate bill requiring identification and tracking to return bottles.
Yes--an emergency bill... for bottles.
**🚨 Millions Lost--So an Emergency Action for Bottles? YES**
Connecticut lawmakers acted quickly to stop "recycling tourism," where out-of-state individuals bring cans and bottles into Connecticut to cash in on the state's 10-cent deposit.
Why the urgency?
Because millions of dollars have been lost, with the burden falling heavily on Connecticut distributors, who are forced to fund a broken system.
The response:
* Emergency legislation
* Mandatory tracking and reporting of large returns
* ID requirements for high-volume bottle redemptions
* Increased penalties and enforcement

Because when it comes to financial losses, fraud matters (Sometimes).
**🏛 ️ Even Opponents Say the System Is Broken**
Even critics of the legislation agree: the system is failing.
[Rep. Tom O'Dea](https://substack.com/redirect/a5c1f1b3-3d7b-4b96-a930-55161d18890e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has argued the current approach may not solve the root problem, suggesting alternatives like reducing the deposit or restructuring the system entirely.
The takeaway is for Connecticut is clear:
* Fraud is real
* The financial damage is real
* Enforcement is necessary

The only debate is how to fix it--not whether it needs fixing.
**The 5 ¢ Question: Could This Be Fixed?**
Some have proposed a simple solution: reduce the deposit back to 5 cents.
The logic is straightforward:
* The fraud exists because Connecticut pays more than neighboring states for bottles
* That price difference creates an arbitrage opportunity
* Lower the deposit, and the incentive to truck bottles across state lines largely disappears

In other words:
👉 No profit -> no scheme
Does anyone remember the Seinfeld episode where Kramer and Newman drove to Michigan for the bottles - this was raised by [State Senator and Gubernatorial Candidate Ryan Fazio](https://substack.com/redirect/8a6ed556-e946-4756-ab7d-a7e72c44a075?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
[](https://substack.com/redirect/1b681911-c324-4eb5-a5ff-b5d57960ef71?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Source CT Senate Republicans](https://substack.com/redirect/a1ce5061-dae0-4b0c-acec-0b0cc2ddf269?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
What this debate really shows is something more important:
👉 Lawmakers are willing to rethink incentives, enforcement, and system design
👉 Because fraud in bottles is taken seriously
**♻ ️ SAVE the Bottles... Ignore the Ballots?**
In Connecticut today (with this legislation):
* You need verification to SAVE the bottles ♻️
* But not to SAVE our elections 🗳️

The state demands ID and tracking to protect a 10-cent deposit...
But calls it oppressive to verify citizenship to protect the integrity of the ballot.
* That's not equity.
* That's not logic.
* That's hypocrisy.

**A Bottle Has More Protection Than a Ballot**
To redeem large quantities of bottles, the state requires:
* Identification
* Tracking
* Oversight
* Enforcement

**But for voting --one of the most fundamental rights in our democracy--verification is treated differently.**
We verify identity for:
* Flying
* Banking
* Employment
* Government services
* Even bottles

But when it comes to voting, verification becomes controversial.
**🗳 ️ The SAVE Act: A Simple Question**
The SAVE Act requires proof of citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.
That raises a simple question:
"Fraud matters--just not at the ballot box?"
**⚖ ️ One Standard--or Two?**
If ID and enforcement are necessary to prevent fraud in a bottle redemption system,
why is it controversial for elections?
**The Bottom Line**
This isn't about left or right as most of the country believes in Voter ID.
It's about consistency.
"Protect the 10¢. Question the vote."
If Connecticut can act urgently to protect distributors losing millions, it can act to protect the integrity of our elections.
If it's worth protecting 10 cents,
it's worth protecting your vote.
**Final Thought**
In Connecticut, bottles get more verification than ballots.

**Peter - as we close out National LGBTQ Health Awareness Week, I wanted to share a piece of my story with you.**

I came of age as a gay man at the height of the AIDS epidemic, a time that can only be described as a mass die-off of LGBTQ people. While our community was fighting for its very survival, the federal government ignored the health crisis since it impacted “undesirables.”

I stayed closeted until 1990, when I came out in college and volunteered on an AIDS hotline. I listened to terrified callers, people newly diagnosed or recently exposed, or trying to care for loved ones who were dying. It took everything in me to stay composed in the face of so much grief and desperation.

Years later, while serving as a San Francisco Supervisor, _I became the first elected official in the country to publicly share that I take PrEP_ , a medication that dramatically reduces the risk of HIV infection. I wanted people to see prevention as health care and to empower others to protect themselves without shame.

**Since then, after becoming a California State Senator, we’ve made real progress.**

I authored legislation allowing pharmacists to provide PrEP without a doctor’s prescription. We required the state to finally collect LGBTQ health data so our needs could no longer be ignored. We made California a refuge for trans youth and their families seeking gender-affirming care. And we strengthened protections so LGBTQ people cannot be denied care, housing, or dignity as they age.

**But today, we’re watching history repeat itself.**

Trump and his allies have launched relentless attacks on LGBTQ health and equality - slashing hundreds of millions of dollars for research into cancers, viruses, and STIs affecting our community, eliminating specialized LGBTQ counselors from the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, making it harder for people to receive lifesaving gender-affirming care, and even banning the federal recognition of World AIDs day.

These decisions will cost lives. People living with HIV will get sicker. Prevention efforts will weaken. LGBTQ young people will feel more alone and more at risk. And this is all part of a campaign to strip away our rights, our dignity, and our very existence.

San Francisco has always been the beating heart of America’s LGBTQ movement, and our community is once again on the front lines of a national fight for survival and dignity.

**We need courageous representatives who understand what’s at stake - and who know how to turn urgency into action that saves lives. That’s why I’m running for Congress.

clean_body: | | Peter - as we close out National LGBTQ Health Awareness Week, I wanted to share a piece of my story with you. I came of age as a gay man at the height of the AIDS epidemic, a time that can only be described as a mass die-off of LGBTQ people. While our community was fighting for its very survival, the federal government ignored the health crisis since it impacted “undesirables.” I stayed closeted until 1990, when I came out in college and volunteered on an AIDS hotline. I listened to terrified callers, people newly diagnosed or recently exposed, or trying to care for loved ones who were dying. It took everything in me to stay composed in the face of so much grief and desperation. Years later, while serving as a San Francisco Supervisor, I became the first elected official in the country to publicly share that I take PrEP , a medication that dramatically reduces the risk of HIV infection. I wanted people to see prevention as health care and to empower others to protect themselves without shame. Since then, after becoming a California State Senator, we’ve made real progress. I authored legislation allowing pharmacists to provide PrEP without a doctor’s prescription. We required the state to finally collect LGBTQ health data so our needs could no longer be ignored. We made California a refuge for trans youth and their families seeking gender-affirming care. And we strengthened protections so LGBTQ people cannot be denied care, housing, or dignity as they age. But today, we’re watching history repeat itself. Trump and his allies have launched relentless attacks on LGBTQ health and equality - slashing hundreds of millions of dollars for research into cancers, viruses, and STIs affecting our community, eliminating specialized LGBTQ counselors from the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, making it harder for people to receive lifesaving gender-affirming care, and even banning the federal recognition of World AIDs day. These decisions will cost lives. People living with HIV will get sicker. Prevention efforts will weaken. LGBTQ young people will feel more alone and more at risk. And this is all part of a campaign to strip away our rights, our dignity, and our very existence. San Francisco has always been the beating heart of America’s LGBTQ movement, and our community is once again on the front lines of a national fight for survival and dignity. We need courageous representatives who understand what’s at stake - and who know how to turn urgency into action that saves lives. ---|---|---
Right now, at a gold-plated beach resort in Florida, one of the richest members of Congress is hosting a two-day fundraiser for himself and charging $3,500 just to get in the door.
Meanwhile, in our part of Pennsylvania, people are losing health care coverage because _that same congressman_ voted to pay for billionaire tax breaks by tripling premiums for thousands of his constituents and kicking people out of Medicaid.
**That 's the deal we get with Dan Meuser. He gets a Florida vacation partying with billionaires, and we get stuck paying their bills.**
[FIRE DAN MEUSER](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/deda236c-e8e7-416a-a31f-ced1668f6e09?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
It doesn't have to be like this. Our representatives are supposed to fight for us. They're not supposed to run away to Mar-a-Lago when people need their help.
And people really do need their representative right now. We get more details every day about just how bad the ICE facilities coming here are going to be for our communities. They'll cost taxpayers $2 million, force a daycare to shut down, and overwhelm local infrastructure so badly that it'll take **[150 poop trucks a day](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/8d6519c0-e036-44a6-a5a9-e1a28f542ecb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to haul the sewage out.
But if you're concerned about any of that - or about rising prices, health care access, or any other issue - good luck. Unless you have $3,500 to spare and a plane ticket to Florida tonight, you won't get any help from Dan Meuser.
I'm running to fight for the people Meuser flat out ignores, but I need your help.
**Our end-of-quarter deadline is 10 days away, and I don 't plan on going to Mar-a-Lago to fundraise before we close the books (or ever). I'm counting on grassroots supporters like you instead.**
**[Can you chip in $35, $13.50, or even $3.50 to help me compete with Meuser's $3,500 Mar-a-Lago checks before the deadline?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/fd167920-d1cf-40ca-8fd2-eac14c6f633f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Thank you, team. I know I can count on you. And you can count on me too.
- Rachel Wallace

Hi, I want to tell you something most people don’t know about political campaigns. When you see a campaign ad on TV or online, it might look simple: 30 seconds, a few shots, a message about what the candidate stands for. But getting that ad on the air is actually a long process. First you write the script. Then you find time to film it, which isn’t always easy when most days I’m traveling across California meeting voters, hearing about their concerns, and talking about the future of our state. **Then comes the final critical piece:[raising the resources to actually put the ads on the air.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127801865/609248805/686976617?refcode=AU_XBCA_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260320_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDcvMS8xMDYyNjIiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZmVmY2QyYjItNjUyNS1mMTExLTlhNDgtMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=2NBO3ndnB2IfwzpRKFJ-YWkgakXFaLz_LKYbv1x6dk4=)** Thanks to grassroots supporters like you, we were able to shoot our first round of ads last week. That’s a huge step forward. **There’s something else you should know.** **I won’t be at the California gubernatorial debate on March 24. Neither will any candidate of color. The host, USC, made sure of that.** **But I have never depended on a debate stage to make my case to Californians. If they won’t give us a stage, we’ll build our own. These ads are how we do it.** I’m running to be governor for the hardest-working and lowest-paid Californians — the people who keep our state running but feel like the deck is stacked against them. My opponents don't have this problem: some of them are backed by billionaires who can flood the airwaves without asking anyone for help. **This moment demands experienced leadership to stand up to the Trump administration and level the playing field for working people. That’s why I’m running — and that’s why getting our message out matters so much right now.** If just a handful of supporters from each of our 58 counties chipped in — even $5 or $10 — we’d have what we need to fully scale up our ad buy and share that message far and wide.
